problem: The paragraph says the classic 8051 and near-clones such as AT89S52 have 4 KB program memory, 128 bytes RAM, two timers and five interrupt sources. AT89S52 is an 8052-type part with 8 KB flash, 256 bytes RAM, three timers and six interrupt sources. The later paragraph even says 8052-type parts have 256 bytes and a third timer, so the text contradicts itself.
fix: Say classic 8051 and 89C51 for 4 KB, 128 bytes, two timers and five sources; say AT89S52 is 8052-type with 8 KB flash, 256 bytes RAM, three timers and six sources.

problem: MOV A,P1 reads the pin state, not the port latch. Only read-modify-write instructions read the latch. Students will get the opposite rule for port input.
fix: Say MOV P1,A writes the port latch, MOV A,P1 reads the pin state, and read-modify-write instructions read the latch.

problem: PSW = 18H is binary 0001 1000, so RS1 = 1 and RS0 = 1. That selects bank 3, not bank 2. The stated base 10H and R5 address 15H are also wrong.
fix: 18H gives RS1 = 1, RS0 = 1, so bank 3. Base = 8 × 3 = 24 = 18H. R5 is at 18H + 5 = 1DH = 29 decimal.

problem: The 8051 has separate program and data address spaces, but it is not pipelined and its external bus is shared/multiplexed. Instruction fetch and data read do not overlap in the classic core. Saying one bus and another and can therefore overlap overstates the architecture.
fix: Say separate address spaces and avoid claiming simultaneous buses or overlap; Harvard here means separate memories, not a dual-bus pipeline.

problem: PSW.1 is commonly the user flag F1, not reserved. Some variants leave it reserved, but standard 8051 tables name F1.
fix: Write bit 1: F1 user flag (reserved on some variants), or just F1 user flag.

problem: The byte at 08H can also be read with indirect addressing by loading a pointer with 08H. Direct addressing is not the only way.
fix: Say it can be read by direct addressing, for example MOV A,08H, or by indirect addressing through a pointer.

problem: P is the parity flag and is updated by hardware. Writing 08H does not force P to 0 when ACC has odd parity, so clears every flag is not exact.
fix: Say it clears CY, AC, F0 and OV and sets RS0; do not say it clears every flag.
